---
title: "05 - Re-align to the xbOstLuri2 chromosome assembly"
output: html_document
---

Re-align all 112 lc-WGS samples to the new *Ostrea lurida* reference,
GCA_061535525.1 xbOstLuri2 (USDA-ARS / PSRF, chromosome-level, 10 chromosomes,
1.03 Gb, released on NCBI 2026-09-21). The step 01 BAMs and VCFs were built
against Olurida_v081, a scaffold assembly with 466,560 sequences and a 12.9 kb
N50, so every downstream genetic result should move to these BAMs.

Differences from the step 01 alignment, both standard for lc-WGS:

- Duplicates are marked with `samtools markdup` (flag 1024, not removed), so
  downstream tools can drop them. Step 01 never marked duplicates.
- Each BAM carries `@RG` with `ID`, `SM`, `LB` and `PL`, so bcftools, ANGSD and
  PLINK name samples by ID.

Inputs and outputs:

- Input reads: `data/raw/*.fastq.gz` (restored from gannet below if missing)
- Input genome: `data/genome/GCA_061535525.1_xbOstLuri2_USDA-ARS_PSRF_primary_genomic.fna`
- Sample sheet: `output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/sample_metadata.tsv` (step 01 derives
  `sample_id` and `location` from the FASTQ names; this step reuses it rather than re-deriving)
- Output BAMs: `output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2/alignments/` (gitignored)
- Output reference and indices: `output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2/reference/` (gitignored)
- Output metrics, figure, logs, `metadata.json`: `output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2/`

Tools come from the Roberts Lab container
`/mmfs1/gscratch/srlab/containers/srlab-R4.4-bioinformatics-container-c3d3116.sif`
(bwa 0.7.19-r1273, samtools 1.20). Nothing needs to be installed.

Every heavy chunk submits a SLURM job on `coenv` / `cpu-g2` and returns at once,
writing the job id to `output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2/tmp/<name>.jobid`. Chunks
skip work whose outputs already exist, so rerunning the file picks up where it
left off. The alignment array waits on the restore and index jobs through a
SLURM dependency, so all three can be submitted in one sitting. Use the
`status` chunk to watch progress and run the summary chunks once every sample
has a BAM.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Paths are relative to code/, so chunks work the same run one at a time or knitted
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE)
```

# Directories

```{bash dirs}
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p ../output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2/{reference,alignments,metrics/per_sample,figures,logs,tmp}
ls ../output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2
```

# Restore FASTQs from gannet

`data/raw/` is not tracked and gets purged from scrubbed storage. The full set
(224 files, 526 GB) is on the gannet web backup. This checks every file named
in the sample sheet against the server's size and downloads whatever is missing
or incomplete, six streams at a time on a compute node. Complete files are left
alone, and `wget -c` resumes partial ones.

```{bash restore-fastq}
set -euo pipefail
repo=$(cd .. && pwd)
out=output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2
sheet=output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/sample_metadata.tsv
gannet=https://gannet.fish.washington.edu/v1_web/owlshell/bu-github/oly-lc-WGS

cd "${repo}"
mkdir -p data/raw
tail -n +2 "${sheet}" | cut -f3,4 | tr '\t' '\n' | sort -u > ${out}/tmp/fastq_expected.txt

# Which files are missing or smaller than on gannet? (parallel HEAD requests)
: > ${out}/tmp/fastq_needed.txt
xargs -P 16 -I{} bash -c '
  f={}; url="'"${gannet}"'/$f"
  remote=$(curl -sI -m 60 "$url" | awk "tolower(\$1)==\"content-length:\" {gsub(\"\r\",\"\",\$2); print \$2}")
  local=$(stat -c %s "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [[ -n "$remote" && "$local" == "$remote" ]] || echo "$f"
' < ${out}/tmp/fastq_expected.txt > ${out}/tmp/fastq_needed.txt

needed=$(wc -l < ${out}/tmp/fastq_needed.txt)
echo "FASTQs expected: $(wc -l < ${out}/tmp/fastq_expected.txt); missing or incomplete: ${needed}"
if [[ "${needed}" -eq 0 ]]; then
  rm -f ${out}/tmp/restore-fastq.jobid
  exit 0
fi

cat > ${out}/tmp/restore_fastq.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=oly-restore-fastq
#SBATCH --account=coenv
#SBATCH --partition=cpu-g2
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --output=${repo}/${out}/logs/restore_fastq_%j.out
#SBATCH --chdir=${repo}
set -uo pipefail
echo "start \$(date -u +%FT%TZ) host \$(hostname)"
xargs -P 6 -I{} wget -c -nv --tries=10 --timeout=120 --waitretry=30 -P data/raw "${gannet}/{}" \
  < ${out}/tmp/fastq_needed.txt
# verify sizes
bad=0
while read -r f; do
  remote=\$(curl -sI -m 60 "${gannet}/\$f" | awk 'tolower(\$1)=="content-length:" {gsub("\r","",\$2); print \$2}')
  local=\$(stat -c %s "\$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [[ "\$local" == "\$remote" ]] || { echo "MISMATCH \$f local=\$local remote=\$remote"; bad=1; }
done < ${out}/tmp/fastq_needed.txt
echo "end \$(date -u +%FT%TZ) mismatches=\${bad}"
exit \${bad}
EOF

jid=$(sbatch --parsable ${out}/tmp/restore_fastq.sh)
echo "${jid}" > ${out}/tmp/restore-fastq.jobid
echo "submitted restore job ${jid} for ${needed} files; log: ${out}/logs/restore_fastq_${jid}.out"
```

# Index the genome

Symlinks the NCBI FASTA into the step's `reference/` directory and builds the
BWA index, `faidx` index and sequence dictionary there, leaving `data/` untouched
(same layout as step 01). `bwa index` is single-threaded and takes roughly an hour
for 1 Gb.

```{bash index-genome}
set -euo pipefail
repo=$(cd .. && pwd)
out=output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2
genome=GCA_061535525.1_xbOstLuri2_USDA-ARS_PSRF_primary_genomic.fna
container=/mmfs1/gscratch/srlab/containers/srlab-R4.4-bioinformatics-container-c3d3116.sif

cd "${repo}"
[[ -s data/genome/${genome} ]] || { echo "data/genome/${genome} is missing; download it from NCBI first" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ -e ${out}/reference/${genome} ]] || ln -s ../../../data/genome/${genome} ${out}/reference/${genome}

done=1
for ext in amb ann bwt pac sa fai; do [[ -s ${out}/reference/${genome}.${ext} ]] || done=0; done
[[ -s ${out}/reference/${genome%.fna}.dict ]] || done=0
if [[ "${done}" -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "index already built, skipping"
  rm -f ${out}/tmp/index-genome.jobid
  exit 0
fi

cat > ${out}/tmp/index_genome.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=oly-index
#SBATCH --account=coenv
#SBATCH --partition=cpu-g2
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=6:00:00
#SBATCH --output=${repo}/${out}/logs/index_genome_%j.out
#SBATCH --chdir=${repo}
set -euo pipefail
module load apptainer
echo "start \$(date -u +%FT%TZ) host \$(hostname)"
apptainer exec --bind /mmfs1 ${container} bash -c '
  set -euo pipefail
  cd ${out}/reference
  bwa index ${genome}
  samtools faidx ${genome}
  samtools dict ${genome} -o ${genome%.fna}.dict
'
echo "end \$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
EOF

jid=$(sbatch --parsable ${out}/tmp/index_genome.sh)
echo "${jid}" > ${out}/tmp/index-genome.jobid
echo "submitted index job ${jid}; log: ${out}/logs/index_genome_${jid}.out"
```

# Align

One SLURM array task per sample, 24 running at once, 16 cores and 40 GB each.
Per sample:

```
bwa mem -t 16 -R '@RG...' genome R1 R2 \
  | samtools fixmate -m | samtools sort | samtools markdup
samtools index; samtools flagstat; samtools coverage
```

A sample is skipped when its `metrics/per_sample/<sample>.coverage.tsv` exists
and is newer than its BAM, which is the last thing the task writes. The BAM is
written as `.part` and renamed on success, so a task killed mid-way never
leaves a BAM that looks finished. Rerun this chunk to redo failed samples.

The array is submitted with `--dependency=afterok` on the restore and index jobs
if either is still queued or running. About 45 M read pairs per sample against a
1 Gb genome takes on the order of 1 to 2 hours per task.

```{bash align}
set -euo pipefail
repo=$(cd .. && pwd)
out=output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2
genome=GCA_061535525.1_xbOstLuri2_USDA-ARS_PSRF_primary_genomic.fna
sheet=output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/sample_metadata.tsv
container=/mmfs1/gscratch/srlab/containers/srlab-R4.4-bioinformatics-container-c3d3116.sif
max_concurrent=24

cd "${repo}"
n=$(($(wc -l < "${sheet}") - 1))
echo "samples in sheet: ${n}"

# Wait on prerequisite jobs that are still in the queue
deps=()
for name in restore-fastq index-genome; do
  f=${out}/tmp/${name}.jobid
  if [[ -s "${f}" ]] && squeue -h -j "$(cat "${f}")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -n "$(squeue -h -j "$(cat "${f}")")" ]]; then
    deps+=("$(cat "${f}")")
  fi
done
dep_arg=""
if [[ ${#deps[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  dep_arg="--dependency=afterok:$(IFS=:; echo "${deps[*]}")"
  echo "will wait for job(s): ${deps[*]}"
fi

cat > ${out}/tmp/align_array.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=oly-align
#SBATCH --account=coenv
#SBATCH --partition=cpu-g2
#SBATCH --array=0-$((n - 1))%${max_concurrent}
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=16
#SBATCH --mem=40G
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --output=${repo}/${out}/logs/align_%A_%a.out
#SBATCH --chdir=${repo}
set -euo pipefail
module load apptainer

line=\$(sed -n "\$((SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID + 2))p" ${sheet})
IFS=\$'\t' read -r sample location r1 r2 <<< "\${line}"
bam=${out}/alignments/\${sample}.sorted.bam
per=${out}/metrics/per_sample
tmp=${out}/tmp/\${sample}
echo "start \$(date -u +%FT%TZ) host \$(hostname) sample=\${sample} location=\${location}"

if [[ -s "\${bam}" && -s "\${bam}.bai" && -s "\${per}/\${sample}.coverage.tsv" && "\${per}/\${sample}.coverage.tsv" -nt "\${bam}" ]]; then
  echo "\${sample}: already aligned, skipping"; exit 0
fi
for f in "\${r1}" "\${r2}"; do [[ -s "\$f" ]] || { echo "missing \$f" >&2; exit 1; }; done
mkdir -p "\${tmp}" "\${per}"
export sample bam per tmp r1 r2   # read inside the container shell below

apptainer exec --bind /mmfs1 ${container} bash -c '
  set -euo pipefail
  ref=${out}/reference/${genome}
  bwa mem -t 16 -R "@RG\\tID:\${sample}\\tSM:\${sample}\\tLB:\${sample}\\tPL:ILLUMINA" "\${ref}" "\${r1}" "\${r2}" \\
    | samtools fixmate -m -@ 4 - - \\
    | samtools sort -@ 8 -m 1G -T "\${tmp}/sort" - \\
    | samtools markdup -@ 4 -s -f "\${per}/\${sample}.markdup.txt" - "\${bam}.part"
  mv "\${bam}.part" "\${bam}"
  samtools index -@ 16 "\${bam}"
  samtools flagstat -@ 16 -O tsv "\${bam}" > "\${per}/\${sample}.flagstat.tsv"
  samtools coverage "\${bam}" > "\${per}/\${sample}.coverage.tsv"
'
rm -rf "\${tmp}"
echo "end \$(date -u +%FT%TZ) sample=\${sample}"
EOF

jid=$(sbatch --parsable ${dep_arg} ${out}/tmp/align_array.sh)
echo "${jid}" > ${out}/tmp/align.jobid
echo "submitted alignment array ${jid} (${n} tasks, ${max_concurrent} at a time); logs: ${out}/logs/align_${jid}_*.out"
```

# Status

```{bash status}
set -uo pipefail
out=../output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2
for name in restore-fastq index-genome align; do
  f=${out}/tmp/${name}.jobid
  [[ -s "$f" ]] || continue
  jid=$(cat "$f")
  printf "%-14s job %-10s " "$name" "$jid"
  squeue -h -j "$jid" -o "%T" 2>/dev/null | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '
  echo
done
sheet=../output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/sample_metadata.tsv
n=$(($(wc -l < "$sheet") - 1))
echo "BAMs finished: $(find ${out}/metrics/per_sample -name "*.coverage.tsv" -size +0 2>/dev/null | wc -l) / ${n}"
grep -l -E "Error|error|Killed|OOM|No space" ${out}/logs/align_*.out 2>/dev/null | head
```

# Alignment summary

Runs once every sample has a BAM. Combines the per-sample `flagstat` and
`coverage` output into two tables and compares depth and mapping quality with
the Olurida_v081 alignments from step 01.

```{r coverage-summary}
out <- "../output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2"
sheet <- read.delim("../output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/sample_metadata.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

cov_files <- file.path(out, "metrics/per_sample", paste0(sheet$sample_id, ".coverage.tsv"))
done <- file.exists(cov_files) & file.size(cov_files) > 0
if (!all(done)) {
  stop(sum(!done), " sample(s) not aligned yet: ", paste(head(sheet$sample_id[!done], 10), collapse = ", "))
}

summarize_sample <- function(sample) {
  cov <- read.delim(file.path(out, "metrics/per_sample", paste0(sample, ".coverage.tsv")), comment.char = "", check.names = FALSE)
  names(cov)[1] <- "rname"
  len <- cov$endpos - cov$startpos + 1
  fs <- read.delim(file.path(out, "metrics/per_sample", paste0(sample, ".flagstat.tsv")), header = FALSE,
                   col.names = c("passed", "failed", "name"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  fs_num <- function(pattern) as.numeric(fs$passed[grep(pattern, fs$name)[1]])
  primary <- fs_num("^primary$")
  data.frame(
    sample_id      = sample,
    numreads       = sum(cov$numreads),
    total_reads    = fs_num("^total"),
    primary_mapped = fs_num("^primary mapped$"),
    mapped_pct     = round(100 * fs_num("^primary mapped$") / primary, 2),
    properly_paired_pct = round(100 * fs_num("^properly paired$") / primary, 2),
    duplicate_pct  = round(100 * fs_num("^primary duplicates$") / primary, 2),
    covbases       = sum(cov$covbases),
    genome_length  = sum(len),
    coverage_pct   = round(100 * sum(cov$covbases) / sum(len), 3),
    meandepth      = round(sum(cov$meandepth * len) / sum(len), 4),
    meanbaseq      = round(sum(cov$meanbaseq * cov$numreads) / max(1, sum(cov$numreads)), 2),
    meanmapq       = round(sum(cov$meanmapq * cov$numreads) / max(1, sum(cov$numreads)), 2)
  )
}

summary_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sheet$sample_id, summarize_sample))
summary_tbl <- merge(sheet[, c("sample_id", "location")], summary_tbl, by = "sample_id")
summary_tbl <- summary_tbl[order(summary_tbl$location, summary_tbl$sample_id), ]
rownames(summary_tbl) <- NULL
write.table(summary_tbl, file.path(out, "metrics/coverage_summary.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

by_location <- aggregate(cbind(meandepth, mapped_pct, duplicate_pct) ~ location, summary_tbl, mean)
by_location$samples <- as.vector(table(summary_tbl$location)[by_location$location])
write.table(by_location, file.path(out, "metrics/coverage_by_location.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# Compare with the Olurida_v081 alignments from step 01
v081 <- read.delim("../output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/coverage_summary.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cmp <- merge(summary_tbl[, c("sample_id", "location", "meandepth", "meanmapq", "mapped_pct")],
             v081[, c("sample_id", "meandepth", "meanmapq")],
             by = "sample_id", suffixes = c("_xbOstLuri2", "_v081"))
cmp$depth_ratio <- round(cmp$meandepth_xbOstLuri2 / cmp$meandepth_v081, 3)
write.table(cmp, file.path(out, "metrics/comparison_v081.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

png(file.path(out, "figures/depth_v081_vs_xbOstLuri2.png"), width = 1600, height = 800, res = 150)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
blank <- cmp$location == "Blank"
plot(cmp$meandepth_v081[!blank], cmp$meandepth_xbOstLuri2[!blank], pch = 19, col = "#3b6ea5",
     xlab = "Mean depth, Olurida_v081", ylab = "Mean depth, xbOstLuri2", main = "Per-sample depth")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
boxplot(mapped_pct ~ location, summary_tbl[!blank, ], las = 2, cex.axis = 0.6, ylab = "Primary reads mapped (%)",
        main = "Mapping rate by location", xlab = "")
dev.off()

summary(cmp[!blank, c("meandepth_v081", "meandepth_xbOstLuri2", "depth_ratio", "meanmapq_v081", "meanmapq_xbOstLuri2")])
by_location
```

![](../output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2/figures/depth_v081_vs_xbOstLuri2.png)

Things to check:

- **meandepth**: non-blank samples averaged 5.3x on v081. The new genome is 10%
  shorter and far less fragmented, so depth should be similar or slightly higher.
- **meanmapq**: should rise. Many v081 contigs were short duplicated fragments
  that pulled MAPQ down.
- **duplicate_pct**: newly available. Anything far above the rest of its plate
  is worth a look before variant calling.
- **Blanks** should still have effectively no reads.

# Metadata

Records parameters, software and the produced files as `metadata.json`, following
`INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Runtime is the summed elapsed time of the alignment array
tasks from `sacct`.

```{bash sacct}
set -uo pipefail
out=../output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2
if [[ -s ${out}/tmp/align.jobid ]]; then
  sacct -j "$(cat ${out}/tmp/align.jobid)" -P --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS --noheader \
    | grep -v -E "\.batch|\.extern" > ${out}/logs/align_sacct.tsv
  echo "array task states:"; cut -d'|' -f2 ${out}/logs/align_sacct.tsv | sort | uniq -c
fi
```

```{r metadata}
out <- "../output/05_realign_xbOstLuri2"
repo_rel <- function(p) sub("^\\.\\./", "", p)

runtime <- NA
sacct_file <- file.path(out, "logs/align_sacct.tsv")
if (file.exists(sacct_file) && file.size(sacct_file) > 0) {
  s <- read.delim(sacct_file, sep = "|", header = FALSE, col.names = c("jobid", "state", "elapsed", "maxrss"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  to_sec <- function(x) {
    d <- ifelse(grepl("-", x), suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("-.*", "", x))), 0)
    hms <- sub(".*-", "", x)
    p <- lapply(strsplit(hms, ":"), as.numeric)
    d * 86400 + sapply(p, function(v) sum(v * 60^(rev(seq_along(v)) - 1)))
  }
  runtime <- sum(to_sec(s$elapsed[s$state == "COMPLETED"]))
}

sheet <- read.delim("../output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/sample_metadata.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bams <- file.path(out, "alignments", paste0(sheet$sample_id, ".sorted.bam"))
metadata <- list(
  script = "05_realign_xbOstLuri2.Rmd",
  date = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
  runtime_seconds = runtime,
  parameters = list(
    genome_accession = "GCA_061535525.1",
    genome_name = "xbOstLuri2 USDA-ARS PSRF primary",
    genome_fasta = "data/genome/GCA_061535525.1_xbOstLuri2_USDA-ARS_PSRF_primary_genomic.fna",
    sample_sheet = "output/01_align_and_visualize/metrics/sample_metadata.tsv",
    aligner = "bwa mem",
    read_group = "@RG ID/SM/LB=<sample_id> PL=ILLUMINA",
    duplicates = "marked with samtools markdup, not removed",
    threads_per_sample = 16,
    memory_per_sample_gb = 40,
    max_concurrent_tasks = 24,
    slurm = list(account = "coenv", partition = "cpu-g2")
  ),
  software = list(
    container = "/mmfs1/gscratch/srlab/containers/srlab-R4.4-bioinformatics-container-c3d3116.sif",
    bwa = "0.7.19-r1273",
    samtools = "1.20",
    R = R.version.string
  ),
  outputs = list(
    alignments = repo_rel(bams[file.exists(bams)]),
    reference = repo_rel(list.files(file.path(out, "reference"), full.names = TRUE)),
    metrics = repo_rel(list.files(file.path(out, "metrics"), pattern = "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)),
    figures = repo_rel(list.files(file.path(out, "figures"), full.names = TRUE))
  )
)
writeLines(jsonlite::toJSON(metadata, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE, na = "null"), file.path(out, "metadata.json"))
cat(readLines(file.path(out, "metadata.json"), n = 25), sep = "\n")
```
